VERDICT: ISSUES
1. `docs/feature/wp4.md:24,110`: The remap contract was changed to `{map_key, mappings}` in `wp3.md:47`, but the UI package plan still says `POST /teams/{team_id}/workflow/remap {mappings}`. Its remap form has no `map_key` input. The UI will send a body the server rejects with 422. The acceptance asked for the UI task description to use the same body.
2. `tests/unit/test_web_workflows_router.py:119-144` and `tests/unit/test_web_mindmaps_work_items_router.py:123-141`: The "foreign team" is a `uuid4()` for a team that doesn't exist, so these tests only show that a missing team gives "team not found". They don't show that a real team the session tenant isn't a member of is refused, which is the authorization-bypass case the acceptance names. A real team owned by another tenant needs to be seeded. I also couldn't run these tests here, because pytest needs approval in this environment.
3. `tests/unit/test_web_workflows_router.py:119-124`: The remap shape test only checks that a body missing `map_key` or `mappings` gives 422. It doesn't pin the accepted body, because it never checks that a valid `{map_key, mappings}` is passed through to `MindmapWorkflowRemapInput`. A wrong rename of the field would still pass.
4. `src/mem_mcp/mindmap/workflow_moves.py:69-80,365-531` and `src/mem_mcp/mcp/tools/_mindmap_common.py:41-61`: Both are uncommitted changes outside the three findings. They add a `SignoffOutcome` / `sign_workflow_move_outcome` refactor and a new `resolve_team_tenant`. Several tools already import `resolve_team_tenant`, so this may be repairing a broken import, but it isn't covered by this work order. It also changes the signoff domain code without any added tests.
